subject: Midterm commit sprint & rate-classification adjustment
messages:
From: Elliot Turner <elliot.turner@novacore.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace Patel <grace.patel@novacore.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — midterm adjustment request

Vanessa —

Thanks for the renewal reminder. We looked at usage through Q3 and want to propose a midterm change: increase our hosted API monthly commit from 1.2T tokens to 2.0T tokens starting Jan 1, 2028, and reclassify our usage tier to unlock a lower per-token rate above 1.5T. We also want a guaranteed burst pocket of 10% for seasonal spikes and a documented soft-throttle behavior (how requests are queued/dropped) so our platform team can prepare fallbacks.

Attached is a short spreadsheet (commit-summary.xlsx) with our forecast and a suggested ramp schedule. Our procurement prefers a single amended SOW and signature via DocuSign. Can your team outline the changes to pricing and any operational guardrails?

Goals: predictable billing cadence, smaller overage exposures, and an SLA note on latency for 95th percentile during normal workload.

-Elliot
VP, Platform Engineering
Novacore AI
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Turner <elliot.turner@novacore.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — midterm adjustment request

Hi Elliot —

Really appreciate the clear forecast and the spreadsheet — that helps. We can support a midterm commit step-up to 2.0T and add a 10% burst pool for seasonal spikes. A couple of clarifying notes before I draft the amendment: 

- Pricing: we can offer a tiered per-token rate: base up to 1.5T at your current rate, and a reduced overage rate for 1.5T–2.0T. Marcus (cc'd) will confirm final numbers and how they affect invoice cadence.
- Soft-throttle semantics: our default is graceful degradation with preferring slower responses over 5xx, and automatic fallback to a quantized model variant if latency SLOs are at risk. We'll document exact behavior in the ops appendix. Hannah, can you detail the fallback steps we should include?
- SLA: we can add a 95th percentile token-latency target for typical payloads; legal will want the SLA language limited to monitoring windows and remediation steps.

Next steps I propose: I’ll put together a one-page MAP (mutual action plan) with milestones (sign SOW, tech runbook, production cutover) and a redline-ready amendment. If that looks good we’ll send a DocuSign link. Can you confirm approval from procurement for a Jan 1 effective date?

Thanks — I’ll aim to share the MAP and proposed-MAP.pdf by EOD Friday.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2027 11:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: pricing & rate-classification options for Novacore

Team —

Looping everyone in to propose the commercials. Summary of what Novacore asked for: 1) monthly commit step-up 1.2T -> 2.0T; 2) tiered rate band to reduce marginal cost above 1.5T; 3) 10% burst; 4) explicit soft-throttle behavior in ops appendix; 5) Jan 1 start.

Proposed commercial path (draft):
- Maintain current base rate up to 1.5T.
- Apply a 12% discounted rate for usage between 1.5T and 2.0T when paid via committed monthly invoice.
- Burst pool: offer a 10% rolling burst available per calendar month; overage beyond commit+burst billed at standard overage rate.
- One-time midpoint onboarding credit of $40k on the first invoice to offset migration/ops work (customers often ask for an onboarding fee credit).

Marcus — need a quick confirmation that the ledger formalizes the 12% as a rate band and how that maps to invoice itemization (monthly line items vs. true-up). Hannah — will ops appendix be OK with the fallback language Vanessa suggested?

I’ll prepare a pricing appendix we can attach to the amendment; want to review before sending externally.

Thanks,
Karthik
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2027 09:45:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Internal: pricing & rate-classification options for Novacore

All —

Confirmed: finance is good with the 12% discount band for 1.5T–2.0T provided it is tied to committed monthly billing (no ad-hoc conversion). We will invoice monthly with two line items: committed tier (flat monthly commit charge) and usage overage/adjustment (true-up). The 40k onboarding credit can be applied as a negative line on Month 1.

Notes:
- Legal will still need to sign off on SLA and chargeback language; keep the SLA remediation steps clear and limit liability to credits rather than indemnities.
- Cash collection: procurement prefers NET30; ok from finance but flag any customer disputes to collections early.

Hannah — anything else operational you need before we finalize the MAP?

Marcus Lin
Director, Finance Ops
From: Elliot Turner <elliot.turner@novacore.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace Patel <grace.patel@novacore.ai>
Date: Mon, 08 Dec 2027 16:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Midterm commit sprint & rate-classification adjustment

Vanessa —

This looks great and aligned. Procurement confirms NET30 and Jan 1 effective date; they also approved the 40k onboarding credit. Ops are happy with the described soft-throttle fallback — Grace will follow up with a short checklist of the failover requirements for the runbook.

Please send the amendment and DocuSign link when ready; Grace will countersign the SOW. Also, include the invoice example (Month 1 with onboarding credit) so our finance team can reconcile.

Thanks everyone for the fast turn — appreciate it.

-Elliot

--
Attachment stubs:
- commit-summary.xlsx (spreadsheet, 32KB)
- proposed-MAP.pdf (pdf, 180KB)
